blockers.what: A name may carry leading, trailing or repeated spaces ('  Claude  ' passes checkAgentName) and is stored and shown verbatim. An HTML page collapses the spaces, so two agents with access whose names differ only by spacing render identically in the agents list; duplicateName and sameNameAgents mark this only while a request waits, not between two agents already paired. Survivable: agentId tells them apart and the request-time marks fire. (/Users/sshlg/DATA/_worktrees/okolos-b1-n-007/apps/agent/src/pairing/name.ts:109-111 and apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:377, found by the `unit` tier)

Pairing.request never looks at the store, so a store that became unreadable after open still takes new requests; SCR-23 (merged in 5ff2e73) and N-008/N-011 acceptance now say POST /pair takes no new request while the access list cannot be read, and N-007 offers no side-effect-free way to ask whether the store reads (N-008 (door /pair), N-011 (createAgent wiring); apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:371-404, found by the `seam` tier)

Pairing stores and shows the NFC form of the name but request() does not return it; spec F6 names the CLI key file clients/<sha256(name)>.key from the name as typed, so a decomposed name (probe: 'Агент И\u0306' passes checkAgentName, raw and NFC hash to different files) gives pair and mcp-stdio --as different files for one agent (N-008 (apps/agent/src/cli/pair.ts, door/stdio-shim.ts), found by the `seam` tier)

N-008 acceptance lists CLI words for five claim refusals (declined, expired, claim_expired, claimed, unknown); ClaimRefusal also has stopped and RequestRefusal has closed, both of which the door can return during a stop (N-008 (CLI pair), found by the `seam` tier)

The service shell has no owner stop hook: with handleSignals, SIGTERM drains, finish() releases the lock and exit(0) runs (http.ts:416-421), so Pairing.close(now) and its stopped notices cannot run before the lock goes; N-011 plans the hook (N-011 (apps/agent/src/service/http.ts:367-438), found by the `seam` tier)

The reload path hands N-011 agent ids (onReload removed: string[]) and revoked notices {agentId, name, at}, never an AgentRecord, while the plan names one type onRevoke(record: AgentRecord); revoke() also sends a revoked notice, so closing tasks on both the notice and onRevoke closes twice; verify() and flush() date reload notices with Date.now(), not the clock createAgent takes (N-011 (agent.ts wiring), N-017 (fake-clock e2e), found by the `seam` tier)

The journal on b1/n-006 (b131f7c) names the agent by name only (AgentCall.agent) and its DoorRejection lacks store_unreadable; Pairing lets two agents share a name (duplicateName and sameNameAgents only warn), so SCR-24 cannot tell them apart without agentId (16 hex) and pairedAt (ms since the epoch, while journal at is ISO) (N-006 (apps/agent/src/journal/journal.ts on b1/n-006), N-015 (refusal line with agentLabel), found by the `seam` tier)

doctor must name an unwritable access list with path and reason; Pairing has no non-mutating writability probe and the errno is only on PairingStoreError.cause (N-016 (okolos-agent doctor), found by the `seam` tier)

docs/privacy.md says its table names every store the product keeps ('их девять') and that all of it lies in the browser and is erased on «Ваши данные». This node defines Okolos Agent's access list, a new on-device file holding agent names, access dates, last-call times and key hashes with no expiry (kept until revoked). It is not reachable yet (tools/reachable.test.ts exempts it), so nothing is false today, but no later node's plan carries a privacy.md check: N-020's tests are only tools/docs.test.ts and tools/runbook.test.ts. Question for the operator: does privacy.md speak for Okolos Agent too? If yes, N-020 owes a row for the access list with its reason for having no expiry. (docs/privacy.md:71, docs/privacy.md:124; apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:38, found by the `product` tier)

Pairing again under the same name with --replace (the advice the shim gives when 'access was revoked or the key is wrong', N-008 plan) gives a second access. claim() leaves any earlier access under that name in place, so when the old key was lost rather than revoked, the list keeps an access whose key no client file holds. The page shows it and the lookalike mark warns, so no documented promise breaks. Question for the operator: should --replace revoke the earlier same-name access, or is a manual revoke on SCR-23 the intended path (and should the page or CLI say so)? (apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:444; spec §11 S5 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-bridge-b1-design.md:307), found by the `product` tier)

When the access list changes on disk (a restore, a hand edit), agents that disappear get a 'revoked' notice and so an event, but agents that appear get access with no notice at all. A Time Machine restore of an older pairings.json would quietly bring back an agent the person revoked (its client key file is not deleted on revoke), and the service events would show the revoke but not the return. Spec §11 F4 puts code running as the person outside Б1's boundary, so this is not a broken promise. Question for the operator: should the events record access that appeared from the file, as they record access that vanished? (apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:194, apps/agent/src/pairing/pairing.ts:593-613, found by the `product` tier)
